v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Introduction

units.source: Before v0.104.0, code executed at renderer level (e.g. front-end scripts) could directly require __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or even Node.js APIs (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__). While this makes them powerful, it also exposes a significant attack surface — any XSS or untrusted script in a note becomes remote code execution on the host.
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Introduction

units.source: To mitigate this, the client-side no longer has access to these APIs and everything must go through the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Electron API__TRILIUM_PH_1__ instead.
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Introduction

units.source: If this API change is causing issues with some of your front-end scripts, consider:
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Introduction

units.source: Interacting with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Backend scripts__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which have a greater degree of freedom.
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Introduction

v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Overview of the API

units.source: The Frontend and Backend APIs reside in a global variable, __TRILIUM_PH_0__, that can be used anywhere in the script. For example, to display a message to the user the following front-end script can be used:
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Overview of the API

units.source: The Electron API is different: it lives on __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (exposed by the desktop preload script), not on __TRILIUM_PH_1__, and is only available in the Electron desktop build. Frontend scripts that use it should guard with __TRILIUM_PH_2__ so they degrade cleanly in the browser and standalone (WASM) builds.
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Overview of the API
v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Additional protection

units.source: Some of the APIs have additional safe-guards built in which prevent unauthorized access.
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Additional protection

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ group is the most heavily validated: __TRILIUM_PH_1__ is restricted to an allowlisted set of URL schemes (blocking __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__, Follina-class schemes, etc.), __TRILIUM_PH_4__ must resolve under the Trilium data directory or temporary directory, and __TRILIUM_PH_5__ is locked to the app's own origin. Invalid input throws on the main side rather than being silently passed through.
units.context: v0.104.0: Disabling the Node integration in Electron > Additional protection
